classification.difficultyReason: Part a requires choosing a useful correspondence across the supplied diagonal and connecting congruent angles to parallel sides; the remaining proofs are scaffolded.

inlines.text: This question reviews proofs by congruence of some diagonal properties of rhombuses and rectangles.
is a quadrilateral with all sides equal.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that: A rhombus is a parallelogram.

spec.description: Unshaded rhombus ABCD with vertical diagonal AC and one matching equality tick on each side. Ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CD=DA; AC is supplied. No parallel marks are given.

answer.short: By SSS, $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle CDA$. Hence $\angle BAC=\angle DCA$ and $\angle BCA=\angle DAC$. Equal alternate angles give $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD\parallel BC$, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked:
In triangles $ABC$ and $CDA$:
$$\begin{aligned}AB&=CD&&\text{(sides of a rhombus)}\\BC&=DA&&\text{(sides of a rhombus)}\\AC&=CA&&\text{(common side)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle CDA$ (SSS).

Hence $\angle BAC=\angle DCA$ and $\angle BCA=\angle DAC$ (matching angles of congruent triangles). Thus $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD\parallel BC$ (equal alternate angles). Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Prove that: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, and bisect the vertex angles through which they pass.

Let the diagonals of the rhombus $APBQ$ meet at $M$.

spec.description: Unshaded rhombus APBQ with both diagonals meeting at M and double equality ticks on all four sides. Ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: AP=PB=BQ=QA; A,M,B and Q,M,P are collinear. No perpendicular or angle-bisector marks are supplied.

answer.worked:
In triangles $APB$ and $AQB$:
$$\begin{aligned}AP&=AQ&&\text{(sides of a rhombus)}\\PB&=QB&&\text{(sides of a rhombus)}\\AB&=AB&&\text{(common side)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle APB\equiv\triangle AQB$ (SSS).

answer.short: $\angle PAM=\angle QAM$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).
answer.worked: $\angle PAB=\angle QAB$ (matching angles of the congruent triangles in part i). Since $A$, $M$ and $B$ are collinear, $\angle PAM=\angle QAM$.

answer.short: $\triangle QAM\equiv\triangle PAM$ (SAS), so $\angle QMA=\angle PMA=90^\circ$. Hence $AM\perp PQ$.
answer.worked:
In triangles $QAM$ and $PAM$:
$$\begin{aligned}AQ&=AP&&\text{(sides of a rhombus)}\\\angle QAM&=\angle PAM&&\text{(part ii)}\\AM&=AM&&\text{(common side)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle QAM\equiv\triangle PAM$ (SAS), so $\angle QMA=\angle PMA$ (matching angles).

These angles lie on the straight line $QP$, so they are supplementary. Hence $\angle QMA=\angle PMA=90^\circ$ and $AM\perp PQ$.

The congruence in part i also shows that $AB$ bisects the angle at $B$. Applying the same SSS argument to triangles $PAQ$ and $PBQ$ shows that $PQ$ bisects the angles at $P$ and $Q$.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Prove that: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal.

Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle with the diagonals joined.

spec.description: Unshaded horizontal rectangle ABCD with both diagonals, four right-angle squares, single parallel arrows on AB and DC, and double arrows on AD and BC. Ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel DC; AD parallel BC; all vertex angles are right angles. Diagonal equality is not marked.

answer.worked:
In triangles $ADC$ and $BCD$:
$$\begin{aligned}AD&=BC&&\text{(opposite sides of a parallelogram)}\\\angle ADC&=\angle BCD=90^\circ&&\text{(rectangle)}\\DC&=CD&&\text{(common side)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle ADC\equiv\triangle BCD$ (SAS).
Since $\triangle ADC\equiv\triangle BCD$, their matching sides $AC$ and $BD$ are equal. Thus the diagonals of the rectangle are equal.
